originality.rationale: The full text of the motivating node-activity Deffuant model supplies the weighted selection law and numerically reported broad trends, not the exact three-person first-interaction absorption law with two confidence cutoffs and opposite activity effects. Finite-graph consensus bounds and heterogeneous-confidence convergence concern different hypotheses and do not mathematically imply this exact distribution. Results database searches returned unrelated three-agent social-choice results and a seven-agent nonfreezing confidence example, not a covering result; residual unindexed priority risk persists.
residual_risks: A small-agent exact first-contact calculation could exist in a less indexed work or supplementary appendix despite no covering result in inspected primary texts.
General random-gossip absorption or bounded-confidence stopping-time theorems could imply the conditional formula after specialization.
Survey DOI 10.1016/j.automatica.2023.111302 was only inspected in accessible scope/excerpts, not its full article; do not infer full-document noncoverage.
The theorem is only for maximal compromise and three agents; one should not infer generic large-network or average effects.

value.rationale: For the smallest nontrivial complete bounded-confidence motif, the theorem gives all terminal laws, two sharp confidence thresholds for possibility and certainty of consensus, and a strict opposite-response result for the same activity increase under mirrored initial opinions. The model paper explicitly motivates studying weight placement relative to opinion; this is a complete natural classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
